problem: Overstates the analysts: the source says the closures made workers interested in risky countries (যাওয়ার আগ্রহ তৈরি), not that they have turned to them; it also covers shrinking (UAE), not only closure.

problem: The shortfall is stated against a cost the reader is never given; the cost figure (AA0203) the arithmetic depends on is missing.

problem: Generalises one office (Gazipur, May 2025) to 'passport offices' and says the brokers are 'outside' the offices, which the facts do not say.

old_str: Brokers sell forged certificates: in 2026 a Chattogram family paid Tk 1,23,000 for a "quick" one that turned out to be fake (see Forged documents and impersonation) [OB0014, OB0015].
new_str: Brokers sell forged certificates: police said a ring, whose arrested members were mainly brokers, took Tk 1,23,000 from a man in Banshkhali, Chattogram, in 2026 on a promise of a quick police clearance and gave him a forged one; his brother said he had a criminal case and so had not applied to the police directly (see Forged documents and impersonation) [OB0012, OB0016, OB0025, OB0026].
problem: Cited facts (OB0014/OB0015) give neither Chattogram nor the 'quick' promise (that is OB0016, police); drops the attribution to the brother and police, and omits that the man had a criminal case and deliberately avoided the normal route, which changes what the case shows.

old_str: Few migrants train first: a Sylhet TTC senior instructor said many who most need training don't come, students with no immediate plan to go abroad come instead, and in the centre's experience about 99% of people go abroad without acquiring a skill [LB0238, LB0239].
new_str: A Sylhet TTC senior instructor said many who most need training don't come, college and university students with no immediate need to go abroad come instead, and in the centre's experience about 99% of people go abroad without acquiring a skill [LB0238, LB0239].
problem: 'Few migrants train first' is the writer's generalisation from one instructor's account; 'no immediate plan' misstates 'no immediate need' (তাৎক্ষণিকভাবে বিদেশে যাওয়ার প্রয়োজন নেই) and drops that they are college and university students.

problem: The cited fact D0024 already answers this: Tk 8,625 is the 5-year super-express fee and Tk 10,350 the 10-year super-express fee, so the Sylhet official was quoting the 10-year rate. The 'Need to know' is not a real gap; if kept, the LB0234 sentence should instead say 'that super express costs Tk 10,350 (the official 10-year super-express fee [D0024])'. If this was the only item in its Need to know block, delete the block header too.

old_str: Brokers sell forged certificates instead: in 2026 a Chattogram family paid Tk 80,000 in advance and the rest of Tk 1,23,000 on delivery for a "quick" clearance that was forged (see Forged documents and impersonation) [OB0014, OB0015].
new_str: Brokers also sell forged certificates: police said a ring, whose arrested members were mainly brokers, took Tk 1,23,000 from a man in Banshkhali, Chattogram, in 2026 on a promise of a quick clearance and gave him a forged one; his brother said the man had a criminal case and so had not applied to the police directly, and that the family paid Tk 80,000 in advance and the rest on delivery (see Forged documents and impersonation) [OB0012, OB0014, OB0015, OB0016, OB0025, OB0026].
problem: OB0014/OB0015 give neither Chattogram nor the 'quick' promise (OB0016, police); drops the attribution to the brother and police; omits that the man had a criminal case and avoided the normal route, so 'instead' wrongly implies an ordinary applicant chose a broker over a slow police process.

section: ### BMET clearance and the smart card

new_str: - According to sources cited by Prothom Alo, 20 smart card applications rejected in the Ami Probashi app (the government's migrant-worker app) between 27 December 2023 and 4 January 2024 were later given clearance; separately, on 31 December 2023 the agency Alif Overseas (RL-847) took out smart cards for 24 Saudi-bound workers for which BMET officials later found no matching data on the server (see Fake BMET cards and fake clearance) [OA0003, OA0016, OA0017].
problem: OA0003 says the 20 applications were rejected in the Ami Probashi app, not issued 'through BMET's own system'; drops the attribution to sources cited by Prothom Alo; merges two separate incidents into one sentence without saying who took out the 24 cards.
